## Domain-Prefixed Epic Numbering

**Problem**: All 8 experts independently used overlapping epic numbers (mostly starting at 30), creating 100+ collisions.

**Solution**: Each domain gets a two-letter prefix. Individual domain files retain their local numbering; this master document provides the global mapping.

| Prefix | Domain | Expert | Detail File |
|--------|--------|--------|-------------|
| **PL** | Core Platform | platform-architect | `platform.md` |
| **NW** | Network & Marketplace | network-architect | `network.md` |
| **SC** | Security & Governance | security-architect | `security.md` |
| **DX** | Developer Experience | devex-architect | `devex.md` |
| **DP** | DePIN & Blockchain | depin-architect | `depin.md` |
| **IF** | Infrastructure & Networking | infra-architect | `infrastructure.md` |
| **DD** | Operational Data Domains | data-architect | `data-domains.md` |
| **PR** | Product Strategy | product-architect | `product.md` |

**Convention**: `PL-01` = Platform domain, Epic 01. `SC-01` = Security domain, Epic 01. All domains use zero-padded sequential numbering starting from 01.

## Critical Path Analysis

The longest sequential dependency chain determines the minimum project duration.

### Critical Path A: Platform → Realtime (14 sprints)

```
PL-01 (Schema) → PL-02 (5th Channel) → PL-07 (Observer Factory)
  → PL-08 (Wire 12 Handlers) → PL-09 (Streaming RPC)
  → PL-12 (Propagation Rules) → PL-19 (Five-Tier Layers)
  → PL-22/23 (Tests)
```

### Critical Path B: DePIN → Full Settlement (15 sprints)

```
DP-17 (Schemas) → DP-01 (Bridge Core) → DP-02 (Merkle Batching)
  → DP-04 (Escrow Contracts) → DP-08 (Oracle)
  → DP-09 (On-Chain Identity) → DP-11 ($TMNL Token)
  → DP-14 (DAO) → DP-15 (Anti-Gaming)
```

### Critical Path C: Infrastructure → Mesh Network (24 sprints)

```
IF-01 (Edge HW) → IF-04 (System Image) → IF-05 (Gateway FW)
  → IF-13 (Reticulum) → IF-14 (SAS/CBRS)
  → IF-16 (LoRa) → IF-17 (Proof-of-Relay)
  → IF-18 (Seed Network) → IF-22 (Atlanta Expansion)
```

### Critical Path D: Security → Full Stack (15 sprints)

```
SC-01 (NATS JWT) → SC-02 (SPIFFE) → SC-03 (AuthZ)
  → SC-04 (Org Identity) → SC-10 (Isolation)
  → SC-17-SC-23 (E2E Stack) → SC-24-SC-27 (Machine Layers)
  → SC-28-SC-32 (Tests)
```

**Bottleneck**: Infrastructure Critical Path C at 24 sprints (sequential), but ~106 SP is firmware/hardware which runs on separate teams. Effective code bottleneck is **DePIN Path B at 15 sprints** and **Security Path D at 15 sprints**.

## Parallelization Strategy

### Stream 1: Platform + Data Domains (concurrent)

- PL phases A-C run while DD phases P0-P1 run
- Both are pure Effect-TS code, same developers
- DD depends on PL schema patterns but not on PL observer system
- **Combined**: 694 SP, 8-10 developers, 14 sprints

### Stream 2: Network + Security (concurrent)

- NW phases A-B run while SC phases A-C run
- SC-10 (isolation) blocks NW-18 (NATS multi-org topology)
- **Combined**: 662 SP, 8-10 developers, 15 sprints

### Stream 3: DePIN + Infrastructure (concurrent)

- IF phases 1-2 (hardware/firmware) run while DP phases 0-2 (schemas/bridge) run
- DP-11 (token) depends on IF-17 (proof-of-relay) for receipt format
- **Combined**: 827 SP, 10-12 developers (mixed HW/SW/Move), 24 sprints (IF sequential, DP 15)

### Stream 4: DevEx + Product (concurrent after Tier 1)

- DX and PR both depend on PL/NW/DD schemas being stable
- Can start after Sprint 3 when schemas are locked
- **Combined**: 599.5 SP, 6-8 developers, 12 sprints

## Entity Ownership Collisions (REQUIRES RESOLUTION)

Three entities are claimed by multiple domains. **One domain must OWN each entity** (Schema → Entity stack). Other domains CONSUME via RPC/HTTP.

| Entity | Claimed By | Resolution |
|--------|-----------|------------|
| **OnboardingSession** | DX-08 (devex) + PR-23 (product) | **RESOLVED: DX-08 owns** full 12-layer entity (56 SP). PR-23 + PR-06 consume via RPC (wizard UI, SLA dashboard). PR drops ~14 SP of duplicated entity definition. Canonical 9-state model from DX. |
| **OrgIdentity** | SC-04/SC-26 (security) + DP-09 (depin) | **RESOLVED: DP-09.1.1 owns on-chain** (Move module, 5 states), **SC-04/SC-24-27 owns off-chain** (12-layer Effect-TS stack). Bidirectional sync: SC→DP best-effort batched, DP→SC <60s SLO. DP-24 reconciliation observer. |
| **TrustChannel** | SC-05/SC-26 (security) + DP-09 (depin) | **RESOLVED: DP-09.2.1 owns on-chain** (8 tier states, subset of SC lifecycle), **SC-05/SC-24-27 owns off-chain** (12-layer stack). On-chain = PROPOSED through PREMIUM/REVOKED only; DISCOVERY/INQUIRY purely off-chain. |

### Action Required

- **devex-architect** and **product-architect**: Resolve OnboardingSession ownership. DX should own entity definition; PR should consume via RPC.
- **security-architect** and **depin-architect**: Confirm the on-chain/off-chain split is intentional and both entities reference each other. Document the mirror synchronization boundary.

## RFC Corrections Found During WBS Analysis

| Finding | Source | Impact |
|---------|--------|--------|
| `Stream.pairwise` does NOT exist | platform deepwiki audit | Use `Stream.zipWithPrevious` everywhere |
| `Entity.make` does NOT accept Machine directly | platform deepwiki audit | Takes `(typeName, rpcs: Rpc.Any[])` |
| Chainlink does NOT support Sui natively (as of Feb 2026) | depin deepwiki audit | Hybrid Pyth + Chainlink-via-EVM required |
| `Seal` framework deployed Jan 2026 | depin research | Available for privacy-preserving settlement |

## Appendix: E2E Stack Template

### Machine-Backed Entity (12 Layers)

```
1.  Schema          — Schema.TaggedClass, branded IDs, filters
2.  Model           — @effect/sql Model derivation, view models
3.  DDL             — CREATE TABLE, TimescaleDB hypertable (if time-series)
4.  Repository      — CRUD + queries, SqlClient integration
5.  Errors          — Data.TaggedError union per entity
6.  L2 Service      — Business logic, computed properties
7.  Machine         — @effect/experimental/Machine with state transitions
8.  ES Handler      — EventLog integration, command→event mapping
9.  Entity          — @effect/cluster/Entity with Rpc.Any[]
10. Observer        — Machine.changes → EntityStateChanged → EventDistribution
11. RPC Group       — RpcGroup.make with streaming RPCs
12. HTTP Routes     — REST API endpoints, OpenAPI schema
```

### CRUD Entity (8 Layers)

```
1.  Schema          — Schema.TaggedStruct/TaggedClass, branded IDs
2.  Model           — @effect/sql Model derivation
3.  DDL             — CREATE TABLE migration
4.  Repository      — CRUD methods
5.  Errors          — TaggedError types
6.  L2 Service      — Business logic
7.  RPC Group       — RpcGroup.make
8.  HTTP Routes     — REST API endpoints
```

### Test Matrix Per Entity

```
T1. Schema unit tests        — 2-3 SP
T2. Repository integration   — 3-5 SP (SQL roundtrip)
T3. Service unit tests       — 2-3 SP
T4. Machine lifecycle tests  — 3-5 SP (Machine-backed only)
T5. ES Handler tests         — 2-3 SP (Machine-backed only)
T6. Observer roundtrip tests — 3-5 SP (Machine-backed only, use it()+runPromise for PubSub)
T7. RPC handler tests        — 2-3 SP
T8. HTTP integration tests   — 2-3 SP
T9. Streaming RPC tests      — 3-5 SP
T10. Property-based tests    — 2-3 SP (Schemas with generators)
T11. E2E scenario tests      — 5-8 SP
T12. ISA-18.2 compliance     — 2-3 SP (regulatory entities only)
```
